To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and implemented two approaches for the polycondensation of polymer chains using DNA hybridization.
DNA hybridization can be used to polymerize triblock copolymer brush chains into nanoworms or crosslinked networks, which can be used to form supramolecular structures.
DNA-functionalized polymer brushes self-assemble to form nanoworms and cross-linked networks, which are analogous to step-growth polymerizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of functional polymers for a range of applications.
the synthesis of polymer brushes with controlled molecular architecture and with the use of these brushes to create new supramolecular structures
the development of new materials based on polymer brushes.

this is the first report on a polycondensation reaction of polymer brushes, and it opens up the door to a new class of supramolecular polymer materials.
the polymer brushes can be used to create supramolecular nanoarchitectures via DNA hybridization, and the process is analogous to step-growth polymerizations.
the DNA-mediated polycondensation of polymer brush chains is a novel and promising approach to the formation of supramolecular nano-objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supramolecular polymerization of polymer brushes can be controlled by tuning the DNA hybridization kinetics, which is a promising strategy to fabricate functional materials.
we were able to use DNA hybridization as a tool to control the assembly of polymer chains into supramolecular nano-structures.
we can control the length and the density of the brushes, the number of the brushes, and the number of the blocks in the brushes by using DNA hybridization.

DNA hybridization can be exploited to form supramolecular polymers from polymer brushes.
polymer brush supramolecular assemblies can be designed and constructed in a predictable manner.
